Writing Python script to calculate the result based on the Wikipedia values and rounding rules. ```python # Let's double check all details: # From Moon page infobox: # Line 19: | periapsis = {{gaps |362 |600}} km
({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km) # The minimum perigee value given on the Moon page: 356,400 km (or 356400 km). # Let's also check if there is any other minimum perigee value on the page (e.g. 356,400 km or 356,375 km or 357,000 km in note). # Line 19 explicitly says: 356,400 km (356 400 km). # Line 73 footnote says: ranging from 357,000 - 407,000 km. # In body text: "The distance between the Moon and Earth varies from around 356,400 km (221,500 mi) (perigee) to 406,700 km (252,700 mi) (apogee)" # Minimum perigee value on the page = 356400 km. # Now Eliud Kipchoge's record-making marathon pace: # Marathon distance: standard marathon is 42.195 km. # Kipchoge's official marathon world record set on 25 September 2022: 2:01:09 (2 hours, 1 minute, 9 seconds = 7269 seconds). # Or 2018 record: 2:01:39 (7299 seconds). # Or INEOS 1:59:40 (7180 seconds - unofficial/exhibition). # Let's test all candidate world record times and perigee values to see if the rounded result in thousand hours changes or remains identical! marathon_km = 42.195 records = { "2022 WR (2:01:09)": 2 * 3600 + 1 * 60 + 9, # 7269 s "2018 WR (2:01:39)": 2 * 3600 + 1 * 60 + 39, # 7299 s "INEOS 1:59 (1:59:40)": 1 * 3600 + 59 * 60 + 40 # 7180 s } perigee_values = [356400, 356000, 357000, 362600] for rec_name, record_sec in records.items(): speed_km_h = marathon_km / (record_sec / 3600) for dist_km in perigee_values: hours = dist_km / speed_km_h th_hours = hours / 1000 round_nearest_1000_hours = round(hours, -3) # or round(th_hours) * 1000 or thousand hours rounded print(f"Rec: {rec_name}, Dist: {dist_km} km -> Speed: {speed_km_h:.4f} km/h, Hours: {hours:.2f}, Thousand Hours: {th_hours:.3f}, Rounded 1000s: {round_nearest_1000_hours}, Rounded k-hours: {round(th_hours)}") ```
